record.paper_title: Progresses on Some Open Problems Related to Infinitely Many Symmetries
record.original_question: For integrable systems with infinitely many generalized symmetries of varying order, why do certain expected orders appear to be absent, and more generally do even-order or fractional-order generalized symmetries exist for standard integrable equations such as KdV and modified KdV?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider integrable nonlinear evolution equations such as the Korteweg–de Vries equation
   u_t = u_{xxx} + 6 u u_x
and the modified Korteweg–de Vries equation
   u_t = u_{xxx} + 6 u^2 u_x.
A generalized symmetry of order N for such an equation is an evolutionary vector field K[u] = K(x,t,u,u_x,u_{xx},...,∂_x^N u) whose flow u_τ = K[u] commutes with the given evolution; equivalently, K satisfies the linearized symmetry condition D_t K = K'[u_t], where K' is the Fréchet derivative. It is classically known that KdV and mKdV each admit an infinite hierarchy of commuting generalized symmetries whose orders form the arithmetic progression {1, 3, 5, 7, ...} of odd positive integers, while symmetries of even positive order are conspicuously absent from the standard hierarchy.

(a) Explain rigorously why, in the standard hierarchies of KdV and mKdV, generalized symmetries of even order do not appear: prove or disprove that no nontrivial generalized symmetry K[u] of even order N exists for these equations (modulo dependence on lower-order symmetries).

(b) More generally, formulate a precise notion of "fractional-order" generalized symmetry (for instance, via pseudo-differential or nonlocal operators, or via a suitable extension of the order grading to non-integer values) and determine whether KdV and mKdV admit nontrivial generalized symmetries of even integer order or of fractional (non-integer) order under this notion.

Provide either an existence construction or a no-go theorem characterizing the admissible orders of generalized symmetries for KdV and mKdV.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent expository work from 2024 lists the question of why certain expected symmetry orders are absent for KdV/mKdV — and whether even-order or fractional-order generalized symmetries exist — as an open problem related to infinitely many symmetries. No definitive proof of nonexistence or construction of such even/fractional-order symmetries appears in the literature; partial results suggest specific arithmetic progressions of missing orders but the general question remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Progresses on some open problems related to infinitely many symmetries
status_evidence.snippet: For well-known equations like KdV and MKdV, there are infinitely many generalized symmetries of odd orders, raising the question of existence of even-order and fractional-order symmetries.
status_evidence.claim: The question of even-order or fractional-order generalized symmetries for KdV and mKdV is listed as an open problem.
